author: Pat Gruner Staff Writer
title: Man pleads guilty to lesser charge in death of Kentrell Haddock - NewsBreak
text: A Greenville man pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter in the 2020 shooting death of a 20-year-old at his home near J.H. Rose High School. Jamoni Keion Edwards, 25, of 137 Waylon Drive, Chocowinity, faces 24-38 months in prison for the March 6, 2020, killing of Kentrell Haddock, 20, in the 400 block of Pittman Drive. Edwards was 20 at the time of the shooting. Assistant Pitt County District Attorney Joel Stadiem said that Edwards has been in prison on other charges as he awaited a hearing in Haddock's death. Stadiem said that on the day of the shooting, Edwards was in the passenger seat of a vehicle with two other people on the way to Haddock's home. He said that Haddock and Edwards had been known to get into fistfights. When they arrived, Haddock went to the driver's side of the vehicle before he came around to where Edwards was seated, opened his door and punched him. Edwards then shot Haddock, Stadiem said. Reports from the time said Greenville police found Haddock dead in the front yard. Stadiem said the vehicle left the scene and went to Charlotte. Edwards was initially charged with an open count of murder in the death. That was reduced to involuntary manslaughter and other charges were dismissed as part of the plea deal. Edwards had previously pleaded guilty to interfering with an electronic monitor and federal gun charges. Haddock's father told Special Superior Court Judge Elizabeth Freshwater-Smith that he now cares for Haddock's 6-year-old son, who talks about his father. He said Haddock died 12 days before his 21st birthday and that he wished the punishment was harsher so that Edwards would have time to "think about" his actions. Haddock's mother also spoke, reciting a passage from Genesis. She said she believed the shooting stemmed from an argument over a woman. Edwards' maximum possible sentence was 59 months. Freshwater-Smith empathized with Haddock's family and assured his father that he would have time to reflect. Tyrell Clemmons, Edwards' attorney, explained that he had taken over his client's case late in its proceedings. He said there were legitimate grounds for a defense prior to the plea deal. Clemmons added that, unbeknownst to him when he took the case, he is related to the Haddocks. He believes that, in time, there will be room for forgiveness, and said Edwards did the right thing in pleading guilty. Subscribe to The Daily Reflector
